Traditional Haitian Spiced Rum

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

Makes about 1 quart (1 liter)Prep 10 min

Rum is a central spirit in Haitian culture and is especially significant during Fete de Papa Zaka, the Feast of the Farmer Loa, where it is offered to honor the spirit of the harvest and agriculture. This traditional spiced rum recipe captures the essence of Haitian flavors and is perfect for celebrating the festival with family and friends.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (480 ml) white rum
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) brown sugar
  • 1 cinnamon stick
  • 3 whole cloves
  • 1 star anise
  • 1 vanilla bean, split lengthwise
  • 1/2 teaspoon grated fresh ginger
  • 1 small piece of dried orange peel

Method

  1. In a clean glass jar, combine the white rum and brown sugar, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
  2. Add the cinnamon stick, cloves, star anise, vanilla bean, grated ginger, and dried orange peel to the jar.
  3. Seal the jar tightly and store it in a cool, dark place for at least 5 days to allow the flavors to infuse, shaking the jar gently once a day.
  4. After 5 days, strain the rum through a fine mesh sieve or cheesecloth to remove the spices and solids.
  5. Transfer the spiced rum to a clean bottle and seal it.
  6. Serve neat, over ice, or use it as a flavorful addition to cocktails during the Fete de Papa Zaka celebrations.

Tips

  • Adjust the amount of brown sugar to taste for a sweeter or drier rum.
  • For a stronger spice flavor, let the rum infuse for up to 2 weeks, tasting periodically.
  • Use high-quality white rum as the base for the best flavor.
